subject: body
title: Drinks and Water
about: Water is the best drink because the body is mostly water and it has no sugar, juice as a sometimes drink and the whole orange over orange juice, soda and sports drinks as sometimes drinks and energy drinks as not for kids, the signs of needing water (dark yellow pee, dry mouth, headache), a water bottle at school, the water in watermelon and soup, plain sparkling water counting as water, warm milk or soy milk in winter, water in winter too, and never sipping from a stream or puddle. NC 1.NPA.1.1 (reasons to drink water), 1.NPA.1.2 (choosing drinks) and 1.PCH.1.1 (germs in untreated water can make you sick). Read it together with a glass of water on the table.
tip: Make him the pee checker: pale yellow means good, dark yellow means go get a drink.

cards.q: Your body is made of lots of water. How much of you is water?
cards.note: More than half of your body is water. It is in your blood, your muscles, even your brain.

cards.q: Why is water the best drink of all?
cards.note: Water has zero sugar and is exactly what your body is thirsty for. Milk is a great drink too.

cards.q: On a hike you see a clear, cold stream. Is it safe to drink from it?
cards.note: Stream, pond and puddle water can carry germs you cannot see, even when it looks clean. Tap water and bottled water have been cleaned, so drink those.

cards.q: Energy drinks are made for grown-ups and have lots of caffeine. Are they for kids?
cards.note: Caffeine can make a kid's heart race and keep you awake. Doctors say energy drinks are never for children; water does the job.

cards.q: Juice has lots of sugar. Is juice an everyday drink or a sometimes drink?
cards.note: Juice has the fruit's sugar without the fiber, so it is a sometimes drink. Whole fruit is the everyday pick, and water is the everyday drink.

cards.q: Which has more fiber, an orange or orange juice?
cards.note: Juice is fruit with the fiber squeezed out. Eat the whole fruit most of the time.

cards.q: What does soda have a whole lot of?
cards.note: A can of soda has about ten spoons of sugar. That is why soda is a sometimes drink.

cards.q: Sports drinks are made for long, hard races. What do kids need at a soccer game?
cards.note: Sports drinks have sugar and salt for long, hard races. For games and playing, water does the job.

cards.q: Your pee is dark yellow. What is your body asking for?
cards.note: Pale yellow pee means you are drinking enough. Dark yellow means drink up.

cards.q: Your mouth feels dry and sticky and your head hurts a little. What might help?
cards.note: A dry mouth, a headache or feeling tired can all mean your body needs water.

cards.q: What do you bring to school so you can sip water all day?
cards.note: Fill it in the morning and refill it at the fountain. Sip at snack, lunch and after recess.
Watermelon, cucumbers, oranges and soup are full of water. Food gives you some water too.

cards.q: In winter it is cold and you hardly sweat. Do you still need water?
cards.note: You lose water by breathing and peeing all year. Dry winter air makes you thirsty too.

cards.q: It is cold outside. Which warm drink is an everyday choice?
cards.note: Warm milk, or warm soy milk if you cannot drink cow's milk, warm water with lemon and a bowl of soup all count. Hot cocoa is a sometimes drink.

cards.q: Plain sparkling water is bubbly but has no sugar. Which is it more like, water or soda?
cards.note: The bubbles are just a gas, so with no sugar added, sparkling water counts as water. Soda is sugar plus bubbles.

cards.q: You wake up in the morning. Your body had no water all night. What is a good first drink?
cards.note: You lose water while you sleep, even just by breathing. A morning drink of water wakes your body up.

cards.q: Plain water feels boring today. What can you add for taste with no sugar?
cards.note: Add lemon, orange, cucumber or berries to water for a little taste with no added sugar.
